stories.title: The Matunga Racket
stories.description: Amit recounts a racket where police would entrap gay men on dating sites, lure them to Matunga station, and then extort money from them, exploiting the stigma and illegality of homosexuality.

stories.title: The Rotenburg Cannibal
stories.description: Amit tells the disturbing story of Armin Meiwes, who advertised for a willing victim to be eaten. Bernd Brandes consented, and the act was carried out on camera. Amit uses this 'icky problem' to discuss the complexities of consent and ethics.

stories.title: Amit's 'Smoking Up' Experience
stories.description: Amit shares that he smoked marijuana once in 1995 with a friend and a famous guitarist but felt nothing, illustrating his personal lack of interest in drugs despite advocating for their legalization.

stories.title: Ajay's Poker Career
stories.description: Ajay mentions his five years as a professional poker player, noting that he never played games against the house (like roulette) because the odds are always against you.

stories.title: Alan Turing's Tragedy
stories.description: Ajay tells the story of Alan Turing, the father of computer science and a war hero, who was persecuted by the British state for homosexuality, leading to his tragic death.

core_ideas.description: A crime should only be defined as an act that infringes on another person's rights. If there is no victim, the state has no business intervening.
Prohibition creates an unholy alliance between moralists (who want to ban 'sin') and criminals (who profit from the black market). Both groups oppose legalization.
Banning goods or services (alcohol, drugs, prostitution) drives them underground, creating a black market where violence, fraud, and coercion thrive.
Prohibition incentivizes criminals to build large, complex organizations (gangs, mafias) to handle the logistics of the black market, rather than operating as small-time 'lone rangers'.
India has limited state capacity. Wasting it on policing victimless crimes diverts resources from essential functions like maintaining law and order and protecting citizens from real harm.

There are ethical dilemmas (like consensual cannibalism or incest) where our moral instincts scream 'wrong', but reason struggles to identify a victim. The state should not legislate based on 'ick factor'.
The most effective way to empower marginalized groups (like women in abusive marriages) is through economic growth and financial independence, which gives them the power to exit.
